subject: Stan compiles this model, but C++ compile fails

messages.author: 2e9423a4b20e1401
messages.subject: Stan compiles this model, but C++ compile fails
parts:
Hi,

I'm doing a simple logistic regression model. To help with vectorization in the gradient computations, I'm building a design matrix and then just using matrix multiplication in the distribution of the response. Stan seems to compile it just fine, but the C++ compilation is crashing. My model is below, and I've attached some of the error (it's from within R and the buffer is being overfilled, so I'm losing the first part). Any idea what's going on here?

Thanks,
Chad

data {
  int<lower=1> N;

  int<lower=1> v1[N];
  int<lower=1> v2[N];
  real<lower=0> v3[N];
  real<lower=0> v4[N];
  real<lower=0> v5[N];
  int<lower=0,upper=1> y[N];
}

transformed data {
  matrix[N,5] x;
  int<lower=1> K;

  K <- dims(x)[2];

  for(n in 1:N) {
    x[n,1] <- log(v1[n]);
    x[n,2] <- log(v2[n]);
    x[n,3] <- log(v3[n]);
    x[n,4] <- log(v4[n]);
    x[n,5] <- log(v5[n]);
  }
}

parameters {
  real a;
  vector[K] b;
  }

model {
  b ~ normal(0,1);
  y ~ bernoulli_logit(a+x*b);
}

messages.author: 2e9423a4b20e1401
messages.subject: Re: Stan compiles this model, but C++ compile fails
parts:
I think I figured it out. The problem seems to come from the line
  K <- dims(x)[2];

I replaced it with
  K <- cols(x);
and it compiles fine now. I'm still not sure why this would be a problem, though. I think this is a bug that allows dims to be applied, for example, to an array of matrices, but not to a single matrix.

The manual says you can do things like dims(y), where y is declared as 
matrix[8,9] y[7];

The result is an array of ints [7,8,9] (and not just [7]). 

Thanks,
Chad
